data_fields.name: luck_die_clamp
data_fields.donor_constant: each die clamped to 1..size after luck

data_fields.name: critical_guard
data_fields.donor_constant: luck cannot make result >= size*dice a crit; capped at size*dice-1

data_fields.name: difficulty_damage_pct
data_fields.donor_constant: DMG row: DEFAULT 0, EASY -50, NORMAL -25, CORE 0, HARD 50, INSANE 100

data_fields.name: wis_luck_bonus
data_fields.donor_constant: pst table: 0 below 15, 1 at 15-17, 2 at 18-24, 3 at 25

data_fields.name: weight_tier_factor
data_fields.donor_constant: 1 within max, 2 within 2x max (half speed), beyond 2x cannot move

data_fields.name: initiative_clamp
data_fields.donor_constant: spdfactor clamped 0..10 after 1d6-4 with negated luck

data_fields.name: resist_out_of_range
data_fields.donor_constant: abs(resist pct) above stat maximum treated as 0

best_idea: A luck-weighted d20 where the defender's luck subtracts from the attacker's, with a critical guard so luck alone can never turn a normal result into a maximum-roll crit.
decision_why: Take the opponent-luck roll and the critical guard, but keep luck as a fight-table stat the server rolls; drop the game-time fatigue clock and the alignment-based weight and damage exemptions, which conflict with one ledger and server-decided outcomes.
acceptance: A server test seeds 10,000 rolls for a luck +3 attacker against a luck 0 defender and asserts a measurable hit-rate shift, that a natural 1 always misses and a natural maximum always crits under the critical flag, and that no luck value turns a non-natural result into a crit.
